info.title: Ferry API
info.description:
The HTTP API of [Ferry](https://github.com/Carter2307/ferry), a self-hosted Render alternative. The `ferry` CLI and the web dashboard use exactly this API.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/v1` route needs the server's API token (printed by `ferryd` on first start, stored in `<data-dir>/api_token`) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; use the **Authorize** button to set it here. `GET` requests may pass it as `?access_token=<token>` instead, because browsers' `EventSource` can't set headers (prefer the header: query strings end up in logs). Webhooks (`/hooks/...`) authenticate with their own secrets, and `/healthz`, this document and Swagger UI need no token.

**Conventions.** JSON bodies with snake_case fields; request bodies reject unknown fields and an empty body counts as `{}`. `{id}` path segments accept a resource id **or** its name. Errors are `ApiErrorBody` documents (`{"error": {"code", "message"}}`) with the matching HTTP status; unknown `/api` routes are JSON 404s. Boolean query flags accept `true/false`, `1/0`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, and an empty value means `true` (`?follow`).

**Streams.** Logs and the change feed are Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`): see the `logs` operations and `GET /api/v1/events`. Idle streams get a `: keep-alive` comment every 15 s, and every stream ends when the server shuts down.

get.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of this API, as JSON. No token needed; Swagger UI at `/api/docs` renders it.

post.description: Creates or updates the services, datastores and env groups a `ferry.yaml` / `render.yaml` describes (nothing is deleted) and queues the deploys that follow. Send the JSON `ApplyBlueprint` request, or the YAML itself with a YAML content type (`application/yaml`, `text/yaml`) and `?dry_run=`. A dry run only reports the planned actions.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Only report what would be done (for raw YAML bodies; JSON bodies can also set `dry_run`).

requestBody.description: The blueprint: a JSON `ApplyBlueprint` request, or raw YAML.

application/yaml.example:
services:
  - type: web
    name: web
    image: nginx:alpine

200.description: What was (or, with `dry_run`, would be) done.

400.description: Invalid body or blueprint (the message points at the problem).

409.description: A resource conflicts with an existing one (e.g. a name used by another kind of resource).

200.description: All datastores with their connection info.

post.description: Creates the row (`creating`) and provisions the container. A failed provisioning still answers 201, with status `failed` and the reason in `error`. Datastores and services share one namespace of names. `memory_limit_mb` (MiB, 16 MiB to 1 TiB) and `cpu_limit` (CPUs, 0.01 to 512, rounded to 0.01) limit the container; omitted or `0` = the server default (see `GET /api/v1/info`).

400.description: Invalid name, version, database, username or resource limits.

200.description: The datastore with its connection info.

delete.description: Removes its container **and its data volume**. Refused while services reference it in their env (`${{datastore.NAME...}}`), unless `force=true`.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete even though services reference it (they will fail to deploy or restart).

400.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON body or query string.

409.description: Services reference it (the message lists them).

patch.description: Every field is optional: `memory_limit_mb` (MiB, 16 MiB to 1 TiB) and `cpu_limit` (CPUs, 0.01 to 512, rounded to 0.01); `0` = back to the server default (see `GET /api/v1/info`). The limits are applied to the datastore's container in place, without a restart, whatever the datastore's status (a memory limit below what the datastore currently uses can fail, or get it killed for running out of memory; a `failed` datastore gets them for its next start). A datastore whose container is not created yet gets them when it is. When applying them fails after they were saved, the error message says so.

400.description: Resource limits out of range.

409.description: The datastore is being deleted (the limits may have been saved).

post.description: Stops a queued or running deploy (status `canceled`); the live deploy keeps serving.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Keep streaming new lines until the deploy or job finishes (instead of only the stored log).

200.description: Server-Sent Events. Every line is an `event: log` whose `data` is a `LogLine` JSON object (see the `LogLine` schema). The stream always ends with `event: end` (empty `data`): once the stored log is replayed, or with `follow=true` once the deploy or job finishes. `: keep-alive` comments every 15 s while idle.

text/event-stream.example:
event: log
data: {"ts":"2026-01-01T12:00:00Z","stream":"system","line":"==> Build succeeded"}

event: end
data:

get.description: Tells a client what changed so it refetches only that: API writes are reported at once, the engine's own changes (deploy progress, datastore provisioning, cron runs) within about a second.

200.description: Server-Sent Events. First `event: ready` (`data: {}`) once the feed watches the store: changes after it are reported, so (re)fetch your data after `ready`. Then one `event: change` per change, whose `data` is a `ChangeEvent` JSON object `{kind, id, service_id, action}`: `kind` is `service`, `deploy`, `datastore`, `env_group` or `job`; `action` is `created`, `updated` or `deleted`; `service_id` is set for services (their own id), deploys and jobs, `null` otherwise. A subscriber that falls behind gets `{"kind": "all", "id": "*", "service_id": null, "action": "resync"}` and should refetch everything. `: keep-alive` comments every 15 s; the stream only ends when the server shuts down.

get.description: Version, base domain, proxy and dashboard URLs, TLS and GitHub webhook status, Docker version. Clients use it to validate a token.

400.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON body or query string.

get.description: Every service with its computed fields. The `state` of live services reflects their running instances (`degraded` when some are down), from counts refreshed at most every few seconds.

post.description: Creates the service with its own variables and env group links, then queues a first deploy (trigger `create`) when it has a repository or an image, unless `deploy` is `false`. Services and datastores share one namespace of names. `memory_limit_mb` (MiB, 16 MiB to 1 TiB) and `cpu_limit` (CPUs, 0.01 to 512, rounded to 0.01) limit every instance and job run of the service; omitted or `0` = the server default (see `GET /api/v1/info`).

400.description: Invalid settings (including resource limits out of range), name, variables or domains, or an unknown env group.

409.description: The name, its default host or a custom domain is already taken.

delete.description: Removes its containers, routes, deploys and variables. Refused while other services reference it in their env (`${{service.NAME...}}`), unless `force=true`.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete even though other services reference it (they will fail to deploy or restart).

400.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON body or query string.

409.description: Other services reference it (the message lists them).

patch.description: Every field is optional; for optional string settings an empty string clears the value. `instances` scales, `suspended` suspends or resumes, `custom_domains` refreshes the routes; build settings take effect on the next deploy. Resource limits (`memory_limit_mb`, `cpu_limit`; `0` = back to the server default) are only saved: they take effect with the next deploy or restart, this request doesn't redeploy. Switching between a git repository and an image requires clearing the other source in the same request. When a side effect fails after the settings were saved, the error message says so.

400.description: Invalid settings (including resource limits out of range).

409.description: A source switch that doesn't clear the old source, or a custom domain another service uses.

post.description: Replaces the secret of the service's deploy hook URL: the old URL stops working, the new one is the returned `deploy_hook_path`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries (default 20, clamped to 1..=500).

400.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON body or query string.

post.description: Queues a manual deploy of the configured source: the branch head (or `commit`) of the repository, or the image. An empty body deploys with the defaults.

400.description: Invalid commit, a commit for a service that doesn't deploy from git, or no source to deploy.

409.description: The service is suspended or being deleted, or the server is shutting down.

post.description: Deploys a `.tar.gz` of the source tree (what `ferry up` sends) to a service without a repository or image; the deploy has trigger `upload` and an `archive` source.

requestBody.description: The raw gzip-compressed tar archive (at most 512 MiB).

schema.description: A gzip-compressed tar archive of the source tree (`.tar.gz`, at most 512 MiB).

400.description: The body isn't a gzip archive.

409.description: The service deploys from a repository or an image: clear its source first.

post.description: Web services and static sites only. The domain is normalized (lowercase, no trailing dot) and must not be used by another service or be a default host.

400.description: Invalid domain, or the service type has no public HTTP.

409.description: The domain is already added, or another service uses it.

404.description: No such service, or the domain isn't one of its custom domains.

get.description: The service's own variables (not those of its env groups).

put.description: The service's own variables become exactly `vars`. They are validated alone and merged with the linked env groups (size limits, `${{...}}` references).

Then restart the affected live services whose effective environment changed (the variables are saved

post.summary: Link an env group to a service
post.description: The group's variables apply from the service's next deploy or restart (its own variables win). Linking an already linked group is a no-op.

400.description: The combined environment would be invalid (sizes).

404.description: No such service or env group.

delete.summary: Unlink an env group from a service

404.description: No such service or env group, or the group isn't linked to it.

get.description: Cron runs and one-off jobs, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries (default 20, clamped to 1..=500).

400.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON body or query string.

post.description: Runs a one-off command (`sh -c`) in a new container from the service's live image. Cron jobs run their own command when `command` is omitted.

400.description: No command for a service that isn't a cron job.

409.description: The service has no live deploy to run from, is suspended or being deleted.

get.description: The merged output of the service's current containers (`instance` names the container). Cron jobs have no long-running containers: their stream is a few `system` lines pointing at the job logs.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Keep the stream open and send new lines as they are written.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Start with at most this many recent lines per container.

200.description: Server-Sent Events. Every line is an `event: log` whose `data` is a `LogLine` JSON object (see the `LogLine` schema). Without `follow` the stream ends with `event: end` (empty `data`) after the recent lines; with `follow=true` it stays open and never sends `end`. `: keep-alive` comments every 15 s while idle.

event: log
data: {"ts":"2026-01-01T12:00:00Z","stream":"system","line":"==> Build succeeded"}

data:

post.description: Rolls out the live deploy's image again (a new deploy with trigger `restart`), picking up changed variables.

409.description: The service has no live deploy yet, or it is suspended or being deleted.

400.description: The deploy belongs to another service, never went live or has no image.

post.description: Sets the number of instances. Cron jobs can't be scaled, and services with a disk run 1 instance.

400.description: Invalid instance count for this service.

post.description: Stops its containers; settings, variables and deploys stay until it is resumed.

get.description: Answers `ok` while the server runs. No token needed.
Same as `POST`, for tools that can only send `GET` requests.

parameters.name: service_id
parameters.description: The service's **id** (names are not accepted: they are guessable).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The service's deploy hook key (part of its `deploy_hook_path`).

202.description: A deploy (trigger `deploy_hook`) was queued; credentials are redacted.

400.description: The service has no source to deploy.

409.description: The service is suspended or being deleted.

post.description: Queues a deploy of the service's configured source. The URL (`deploy_hook_path` of the service) is the secret: no token needed. Rotate it with `POST /api/v1/services/{id}/deploy-hook/rotate`.

parameters.description: The service's **id** (names are not accepted: they are guessable).

parameters.name: key

post.description: Set it up in GitHub with the server's webhook secret (`github_webhook_secret`). A `push` deploys (trigger `webhook`, commit = `after`) every auto-deploy service whose repository and branch match; `ping` answers `{"ok": true}`; other events are ignored. Replayed deliveries (same body or delivery id) are ignored too.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: `sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>` with the webhook secret.

requestBody.description: The event payload: JSON, or form-encoded with the JSON in a `payload` field (GitHub's default content type). At most 25 MiB.

400.description: Invalid payload.

404.description: GitHub webhooks are not enabled (no webhook secret configured).

ApplyBlueprint.description:
`POST /api/v1/blueprints/apply` (JSON body) — or send the raw YAML with
`Content-Type: application/yaml` and `?dry_run=true`.

BlueprintAction.description: One planned/performed change of a blueprint apply.

ChangeEvent.description: One change: the `data` of an `event: change` frame.

id.description: Id of the changed resource (`*` with `resync`).

service_id.description: Set for services (their own id), deploys and jobs (their service); `null` otherwise.

ChangeKind.description: What a change event is about (`all` only with `resync`).

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit, in CPUs. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit, in MiB. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit per instance, in CPUs. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

deploy.description: Queue a first deploy (default: true when repo_url or image is set).

env_groups.description: Env groups to link (ids or names).

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit per instance, in MiB. Omitted or 0 = the server default.

Datastore.description: A managed Postgres or Redis instance (one container + one volume).

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit of the container, in CPUs. `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-cpu-limit`).

host_port.description: Port published on the host for external access (bound to 127.0.0.1).

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit of the container, in MiB. `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-memory-limit`).

name.description: Unique DNS-label name; also the private-network hostname.

version.description: Major version / image tag, e.g. "16" (postgres) or "7" (redis).

external_url.description: Connection string from the Ferry host (published on 127.0.0.1).

internal_url.description: Connection string on the private network (use from services).

DatastoreView.description: A datastore with its connection info.

Deploy.description: One attempt to ship a version of a service.

image.description: Image that was built / pulled / reused. Set once the build succeeds.

port.description:
Container port this deploy's instances listen on (chosen at deploy time
via `env::choose_port`; None for workers / cron jobs).

oneOf.description: Clone `repo_url` at `branch` (or the exact `commit`) and build.
Build from an uploaded `.tar.gz` stored at `path` on the server.
Pull and run a prebuilt image.
Reuse an already-built local image (rollback / restart / env change).

DeploySource.description: Where a deploy's code / image comes from.

EnvGroup.description: A named, reusable set of environment variables linked to services.

EnvGroupView.description: An env group with its variables and linked services.

EnvVar.description:
A plain environment variable. Values may contain references such as
`${{datastore.db.connectionString}}` (see [`crate::env`]).

GithubHookResponse.description:
Response of `POST /hooks/github`: `{"deploys": [...]}` for a push,
`{"deploys": [], "ignored": true, "reason": "..."}` for an already
processed delivery, `{"ok": true}` for `ping` and `{"ignored": true}` for
other events.

deploys.description: Deploys queued by a push (credentials redacted).

ignored.description: The delivery wasn't acted on (not a push, or a replayed push).

InstanceStatus.description: Live container state of one instance.

cpu_limit.description: The container's CPU limit (CPUs); `None` when unlimited.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the last exit, for exited / restarting containers.

memory_limit_bytes.description: The container's memory limit (bytes); `None` when unlimited.

oom_killed.description:
The kernel killed the container's process for exceeding its memory
limit (the last time it exited).

state.description: Docker state: created, running, restarting, exited, dead...

JobRun.description: A cron-job run or one-off job (`ferry run`).

command.description: Command override (`sh -c`), else the service start command / image CMD.

instance.description: Short container/instance identifier for runtime logs (None for build logs).

LogStreamKind.description: Which output a line came from.

command.description: Shell command (`sh -c`). Required for non-cron services.

default_cpu_limit.description: CPU limit (CPUs) of containers that set none. 0 = unlimited.

default_memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit (MiB) of containers that set none. 0 = unlimited.

docker_cpus.description: CPUs of the Docker host, if known.

docker_memory_bytes.description: Total memory of the Docker host (bytes), if known.

auto_deploy.description: Redeploy automatically on git push to `branch`.

branch.description: Branch to build and to watch for auto-deploys.

build_command.description: Build command for native runtimes (e.g. `npm run build`).

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit of each instance (and of the service's jobs), in CPUs
(`0.5` = half a core). `None` = the server default
(`ferryd --default-cpu-limit`). Takes effect with the next deploy or
restart.

custom_domains.description: Extra hostnames routed to this service (web services and static sites).

disk_mount_path.description:
Persistent volume mount path. A service with a disk uses recreate
(stop-then-start) deploys and is limited to one instance.

health_check_path.description: HTTP path that must answer 2xx/3xx before a new deploy receives traffic.

live_deploy_id.description: The deploy currently live, if any.

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit of each instance (and of the service's jobs), in MiB.
`None` = the server default (`ferryd --default-memory-limit`). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

name.description: Unique DNS-label name; also the private-network hostname.

port.description: Container port the app listens on. `None` = auto (see `env::choose_port`).

publish_dir.description: Directory of built files to serve (static sites).

repo_url.description: Git URL (https, ssh, or local path / file://). Mutually exclusive with `image`.

root_dir.description: Subdirectory of the repo used as build context (monorepos).

schedule.description: 5-field cron expression (cron jobs only), evaluated in UTC.

start_command.description: Start command; overrides the image CMD (run via `sh -c`).

deploy_hook_path.description: `POST` here (no auth header needed) to trigger a deploy.

env_groups.description: Names of linked env groups, in link order.

hosts.description: All hostnames routed to the service.

internal_host.description: Hostname on the private network (= name).

internal_port.description: Port of the live deploy (private network), if known.

url.description: Public URL (web services and static sites).

ServiceView.description: A service as returned by the API (the stored row plus computed fields).

SourceArchive.description: A gzip-compressed tar archive of the source tree (`.tar.gz`, at most 512 MiB).

SourceKind.description: Where a service's code comes from (derived from its fields).

UpdateDatastore.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/datastores/{id}` — change resource limits. 0 clears
(server default). Applied to the running container in place (no restart).

cpu_limit.description: CPU limit, in CPUs. 0 clears (server default); omitted keeps it.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit, in MiB. 0 clears (server default); omitted keeps it.

UpdateService.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/services/{id}` — every field optional. For optional string
settings, an empty string clears the value. Changing `instances` scales,
`suspended` suspends/resumes, `custom_domains` refreshes routes; build
settings and resource limits take effect on the next deploy.

cpu_limit.description:
CPU limit per instance, in CPUs. 0 clears (server default). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory limit per instance, in MiB. 0 clears (server default). Takes
effect with the next deploy or restart.

bearer.description: The server's API token (`ferryd` prints it on first start; it is stored in `<data-dir>/api_token`). `GET` requests may send it as `?access_token=` instead.

tags.name: info
tags.description: Server info, liveness and this document.

tags.name: services
tags.description: Web services, private services, background workers, static sites and cron jobs: CRUD, lifecycle actions (restart, suspend, resume, scale, rollback), status and runtime logs.

tags.name: deploys
tags.description: Deploy history, manual deploys, source uploads (`ferry up`), cancellation and build logs.

tags.name: env
tags.description: A service's own environment variables. `?restart=true` restarts the live service when its effective environment changed.

tags.name: env-groups
tags.description: Shared variable sets linked to services (a service's own variables win over its groups'), and linking / unlinking them.

tags.name: domains
tags.description: Custom domains of web services and static sites (unique across services).

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Job runs: cron runs and one-off commands, with their logs.

tags.name: datastores
tags.description: Managed Postgres and Redis instances with their connection strings and resource limits.

tags.name: blueprints
tags.description: Infrastructure as code: apply a `ferry.yaml` / `render.yaml` (idempotent, with a dry run).

tags.name: events
tags.description: The change feed (Server-Sent Events) the web client uses to stay current without polling.

tags.name: hooks
tags.description: Webhooks: secret deploy hook URLs and GitHub push events. They authenticate with their own secrets, never the API token.
